From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Tailwind pilot: initial sizing checklist

Hi Emily —

Great to meet on the call yesterday. Thanks for the walkthrough of Tailwind's inference patterns. To move the dedicated sizing forward on our side we typically ask for a short workload census so we can validate GPU SKU recommendations and quantify burst vs sustained capacity. Can you fill out the items below (a quick copy/paste reply is perfect) and attach a small sample of request telemetry (CSV) if possible? If procurement needs a separate package, loop them in — that's fine.

Quick asks:
- Primary API types (chat/generation/embeddings/rerank): one-line
- Average prompt length (tokens) and typical response length (tokens) per API type
- 95th/99th concurrency targets (peak concurrent sessions or requests)
- Burst window shape: minutes of sustained peak vs short microbursts (seconds)
- Expected percent of calls that use streaming vs non-streaming
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95 target in ms) and cost sensitivity (high/medium/low)

If you can share a 24–72 hour telemetry sample (timestamps, endpoint, prompt_tokens, response_tokens) we'll run a quick token-flow analysis and return a recommended SKUs mix (example: 1x L40 + 4x H100 mix) and an initial throughput/latency projection.

I copied Marissa for ops alignment; she'll lead the sizing workbook after we have telemetry.

Thanks,

Hi Michael —

Thanks for the clear checklist. Answers below (copied Tim for procurement visibility). I've attached a 48-hour sample from our staging cluster (tailwind_telemetry_sample.csv) and a procurement note (procurement_terms.pdf).

Answers: 
- Primary API types: generation (customer-facing chat), embeddings (batch vectorize), and two internal rerank endpoints for search.
- Avg prompt/response tokens:
  - generation/chat: prompt 85 tokens, response 210 tokens (median); 99th response ~900 tokens
  - embeddings (bulk): prompt 120 tokens, response = vector only (no text)
  - rerank: prompt 35 tokens, response 18 tokens
- Concurrency targets:
  - steady-state concurrent requests: ~160
  - 95th concurrent: 420
  - 99th concurrent (short spikes during marketing events): ~1,100 for 30–120s
- Burst window shape: daily marketing spikes (~10–15 min sustained at 99th), microbursts of 20–90s with higher peak.
- Streaming percent: generation uses streaming ~62% of calls, rest non-streaming. Embeddings non-streaming (batch).
- Latency SLOs: p50 120ms (generation token-level), p95 450ms (token-level), hard p99 <= 1,200ms for interactive paths; cost sensitivity: medium.

Additional notes: we use session affinity for chat (sticky to GPU for a session), and KV cache hit is expected ~18% for repeated prompts during a session. We can provide annotation on endpoints column in the CSV if helpful.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if you need clarifications.

Best,
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Engineering
Neutrino Labs
emily.zhao@neutrinolabs.com

Subject: Tailwind pilot: internal sizing notes + next steps

Marissa / Karthik —

Following Emily's telemetry and answers, I ingested the 48-hour CSV and ran a quick token-flow pass. High-level findings (summary for the internal sizing workbook):

- Traffic mix: generation/chat ~72% of token volume, embeddings 18% (batch windows concentrated 02:00–05:00 UTC), rerank 10%
- Token distribution: median response 210 tokens for chat; 99th ~900 tokens — results in large variance in per-request token cost.
- Concurrency: sustained ~160, peaks up to ~1,100 for short bursts. Burst energy is concentrated in a 10–15 minute marketing window, with microburst hotspots at campaign kickoffs.

Prelim recommendation (very conservative pilot reserve for 3 months):
- Primary mix: 2x L40 (for streaming-heavy generation, better token throughput) + 6x H100 80GB (for high concurrency and long-response tail)
- Autoscale policy: hold a hot pool for the first 250 concurrent sessions; additional capacity to scale within 60s for short spikes (fast autoscale + pre-warming for predicted campaign windows)
- KV cache plan: enable prefix caching; with ~18% hit we estimate 12–15% token reduction during sessions — include cache warming during campaign prep
- Quantization: Karthik to validate mixed-precision float16 + int8 packing on the generation model; expect 8–12% additional throughput if safe for quality

Action items: 
- Marissa: prepare a formal sizing workbook (workbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-tailwind-pilot) and draft reserved capacity quote for 3 months (include burst credit clause).
- Karthik: run validation pass on model quantization profile and provide expected p95 improvement and any quality risk notes.
- Michael: prepare a short slide for Emily summarizing the SKU mix + quick cost estimate per 1k tokens.

I'll send the customer-facing sizing summary once we have Karthik's quant results and Marissa's workbook. Emily / Tim — expect the sizing brief by Friday. If you want an ops review call, propose a slot and we'll join.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
